image_description: The image displays the dorsal surface of a large crocodilian swimming in rippled water. Only the top of the head, the ridged back, and the upper portion of the tail are visible above the waterline. The skin appears dark, textured, and armored with osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the snout emerging from the water shows a tapered, V-shaped profile consistent with a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject's mouth is closed and mostly submerged; individual teeth and the specific interlocking mechanism (4th lower tooth) are not visible due to the viewing angle and water occlusion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the eye bumps are visible on the top of the head, the resolution and distance prevent verification of pupil shape (vertical slit) or the presence of a nictitating membrane.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct nostril protrusions are visible at the very end of the snout, consistent with crocodilian anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible section of the body extending from the neck to the tail base is clearly elongated and covered in heavy, bony armor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of raised, keeled scutes (osteoderms) run longitudinally down the spine, matching the taxonomic description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is dark grey/brown, and the texture appears rough and calcified, consistent with wet crocodile skin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral (belly) side is completely submerged and occluded by the water; this feature cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All limbs are submerged beneath the water surface and are not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the tail shows significant lateral compression (flattened sides) and muscular ridges, typical of aquatic propulsion adaptations.

alignment_reasoning: The image demonstrates high fidelity to the 'African crocodile' class. All testable checkpoints regarding dorsal anatomy (V-shaped snout, nostril placement, longitudinal scute rows, lateral tail compression) are present and accurate. Several checkpoints were marked untestable due to natural occlusion by water (teeth, eyes details, belly, limbs), which is expected for a swimming subject. No anatomical contradictions were found in the visible regions.
artifact_reasoning: No AI-generation artifacts detected. The water ripples exhibit natural fluid dynamics and refraction patterns. The boundary between the crocodile's skin and the water is sharp and physically consistent, with no melting, bleeding, or texture anomalies. Lighting and shadows on the wet skin are realistic.
